description_full: Valaris Limited, together with its subsidiaries, provides offshore contract drilling services in Brazil, the United Kingdom, Gulf of America, Australia, Angola, and internationally. It operates through four segments: Floaters, Jackups, ARO, and Other. The company owns an offshore drilling rig fleet, which includes drillships, dynamically positioned semisubmersible rigs, a moored semisubmersible rig, and jackup rigs. It also offers management services on rigs owned by third parties. The company serves international, government-owned, and independent oil and gas companies. Valaris Limited was founded in 1975 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.

financial_summary: Valaris Limited is a mid-cap energy business with a $5.8B market cap on $2.4B of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at +14% over the past three years and -5% annually across the full decade, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder.
Returns on capital run at 3% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests.

The business throws off $203M in free cash flow — roughly 9 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.56×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
Accruals are elevated at +8.2% of assets, and Sloan showed firms building earnings through accruals rather than cash systematically underperform.
On the balance sheet, leverage is comfortably conservative at 0.8× net debt/EBITDA, and interest coverage runs at 5.3×.

Shareholder yield is only 1.7%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 12% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and within its sector the business captures 1.8× its fair share of profits, a structural advantage visible in the numbers.
